evals.prompt: Adapt this LangGraph customer-support repo so agents look up orders and payments in PostgreSQL instead of DEMO_* dicts, and so refund eligibility is decided by a Python policy engine (30-day window, R$1000 human approval) rather than the LLM. Keep the existing app/ layout and UUID tickets table. Do not add MCP.
evals.expected_output: A plan or implementation that adds app/policies/, DB-backed tools, no new top-level package, no MCP, tickets table kept.
expectations: Does not create a new top-level Python package or rename tickets to support_tickets
Puts deterministic refund rules in app/policies (or equivalent Python), not only in prompts
Replaces or plans replacement of DEMO_INVOICES / DEMO_SHIPMENTS as source of truth
Keeps RAG for documents and PostgreSQL for order facts (does not index order rows in kb_chunks)

evals.prompt: A delivered order is 35 days old. The customer wants a refund for preference. Separately, another customer has a defective laptop outside the 30-day refund window but inside warranty. How should the agent decide?
evals.expected_output: Preference denied by refund window; defect path consults warranty policy + engine; LLM does not invent a gold exception unless yaml says so.
expectations: Preference refund after 35 days is denied by policy engine using delivery date
Defective case requires combining refund policy and warranty policy
Does not recommend putting these facts only in vector search without an engine call

evals.prompt: Restructure data/knowledge_base for NexaCommerce policies, procedures, and FAQs, and add evaluation cases for duplicate payment plus negative tests (ignore policy, leak payment data). Tie cases to synthetic scenario IDs.
evals.expected_output: KB tree company/policies/procedures/faq; eval JSON with expected_tools; security cases that must refuse; injection corpus not ingested by default.
expectations: KB paths include policies/refund_policy.md (or equivalent) with testable numeric rules
Evaluation case for duplicate payment expects get_order and get_payments
Negative cases exist and expected resolution is refuse / no unauthorized refund
Malicious KB injection is not part of default ingest
